newsitem.title: JAPAN: INSTANT VIEW - Japan July industrial output data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Japan July industrial output data.

text.p: Japan's industrial output rose a preliminary 4.1 percent in July from the previous month on a seasonally adjusted basis, official data showed on Friday.
Economists polled by Reuters had forecast on average 3.4 percent growth from the previous month. Analysts' comments follow. MASARU TAKAGI, CHIEF ECONOMIST, FUJI RESEARCH INSTITUTE:
"Today's figure is a very strong figure, but the total situation is not so strong."

"Recently, production in the mining and manufacturing sectors is still a case of one step forward and one step back. (Future) figures won't be so brilliant due to the reduced expenditure on public works and poor export performance and rising imports."
NIGEL RICHARDSON, HEAD OF BOND RESEARCH, YAMAICHI INTERNATIONAL EUROPE:

"I'm not that sure that the bond market's reaction is going to be that negative. On the face of it, it should be, because a lot of people were going for something like a 3.4 percent figure. Yesterday we saw numbers coming out for car output and those indicated a very sharp rise, and so I think the market had already begun to steer itself towards a better figure."

"I agree with the overall view we've had so far -- that is, ultimately these figures are really only a bounce back from the previous month's fall. I'm not sure that they are convincing evidence that the recovery is coming through a lot stronger. On that basis a bond market reaction is likely to be a negative bond reaction, but it will be relatively short-lived."
YOZO NISHIMURA, ECONOMIST, BANK OF TOKYO MITSUBISHI:

"The output data shows that the economy lacks strength, but it is still continuing slow recovery. The data confirmed that there are no downward risks in the economy. A bright side is that inventories are moving towards an appropriate level."
